finding.claim: After a block fails validation, decompression, or checksum, LZ4BlockInputStream leaves the read cursor o and finished state unchanged while originalLen has already been overwritten with the attacker's value. A caller that catches the IOException and calls read() again receives bytes from the failed, unverified block, so the integrity check is bypassed for tolerant callers.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled compressed stream bytes: header fields compressedLen/originalLen/check read at LZ4BlockInputStream.java:259-281.
finding.sink: read()/read(byte[],int,int)/available() returning buffer contents of a block whose XXHash32 check failed (LZ4BlockInputStream.java:195-204, 219-221, 190).

trace.note: Header bytes read from untrusted input stream.
originalLen assigned from header BEFORE any validation; field now holds attacker value.
Validation throws IOException on bad header; o and finished are not reset, originalLen stays changed.
Decompression writes attacker-chosen plaintext into buffer (also on LZ4Exception path at 327-329, partially written).
Checksum mismatch throws IOException; buffer already holds the unverified output; o=0 at line 339 never runs.
Next read(): o != originalLen, so refill() is skipped and no re-validation happens.
Returns buffer[o++], i.e. unverified plaintext. read(byte[]) at 219-221 copies from the same buffer; len=min(len, originalLen-o) can go negative after a header failure.

finding.guards_checked: Magic, method, level and size bounds at 268-291 (pass for a crafted header). Checksum verification at 334-338 gates only the return from readBlock, not later reads. No sticky error/finished flag is set on exception. refill gating at 198/213 keys off originalLen, which was already updated. Attacker can craft literal bytes to produce arbitrary plaintext and set a wrong check value. Exploitability depends on the caller catching IOException and continuing; not run, verified by reading.

finding.claim: In LZ4FrameInputStream, frameInfo is replaced with the new frame's unverified FLG/BD values before the descriptor hash is checked. After DESCRIPTOR_HASH_MISMATCH, a caller that retries read() skips nextFrameInfo() and decodes the rejected frame's blocks using its unverified CONTENT_CHECKSUM/BLOCK_CHECKSUM flags and the previous frame's maxBlockSize.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled frame descriptor bytes (FLG, BD, descriptor hash byte) for the second or later frame in a multi-frame stream: LZ4FrameInputStream.java:196-210, 225-228.
finding.sink: Block data emitted to the caller from readBlock (LZ4FrameInputStream.java:356-357), with integrity checks selected by unverified flags (:335, :352) and a stale block bound (:305).

trace.note: this.frameInfo = new FrameInfo(flg, bd, ...) built from untrusted descriptor bytes.

Mismatch throws DESCRIPTOR_HASH_MISMATCH; frameInfo already replaced and not finished (LZ4FrameOutputStream.java:452-458, finished defaults false). firstFrameHeaderRead stays true and maxBlockSize (:242) is never updated.
Retried read(): frameInfo.isFinished() is false, so nextFrameInfo() is skipped and readBlock() runs on the rejected frame.
BLOCK_CHECKSUM taken from the unverified flags, so the attacker can clear it.
Decoded data exposed through buffer to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: Descriptor hash at 232-240 (gates the throw only). Block size check against maxBlockSize at 305 (stale value from the previous frame). Per-block checksum only when BLOCK_CHECKSUM is set by the same unverified flags. Content checksum at 294 is checked only at end of frame. Also: a failed block (checksum/decompress error at 326-338) is consumed and the reader resumes at the next block, so a tolerant caller silently drops it unless CONTENT_CHECKSUM catches it. Requires multi-frame input and a caller that continues after IOException; not run, verified by reading.
